Jon Bonck

Republican candidate for U.S. Representative, District 38, Harris County, Texas · Open seat

Sales manager, Bonck & Baker Mortgage Group (calls himself a small-business owner)

Jon Bonck is a Republican mortgage company sales manager running for the open seat in Texas' 38th Congressional District, which Rep. Wesley Hunt (R) left to run for the U.S. Senate. He finished first in the March 3, 2026 Republican primary and won the May 26 runoff against Shelly deZevallos. In the November 3 general election he faces Melissa McDonough (D) and Alex McMenemy (G).

Where Bonck stands

Immigration / border security
Lists securing the border as a top priority if elected.
Abortion
Lists 'protecting life' among his top priorities.
Guns
Lists protecting the Second Amendment as a priority. Opposes gun regulations and calls carrying a firearm a 'God-given' right.
Education / parental rights
Lists defending parental rights as a top priority.
Religious liberty
Lists protecting religious liberty and restoring 'biblical values' among his priorities.
Health care
Lists 'restoring medical freedom' among his priorities.
Cost of living / economy
Says rising living costs are a key district challenge. Proposes expanding economic opportunity and investing in infrastructure for the district's growing communities.
Government spending
Proposes stopping fraud, waste and abuse in federal government.
Social Security
Supports Social Security reform.
Trump agenda
Says he will advance President Trump's America First agenda. Trump endorsed him on Feb. 16, 2026.

Background

  • Has never held elected office
  • Sales manager, Bonck & Baker Mortgage Group (2019–present)
  • Marketing role, Nalco Champion (from 2015)
  • Earlier worked in quality control in the biochemical and petroleum industries
  • B.S. in biochemistry, Louisiana State University
  • Won 2026 TX-38 Republican primary runoff (May 26, 2026)
